chunk_1.page_content:
Interface Requirements Specification

Sample Network Communication Protocol

Document ID: IRS-NCP-002    |    Version: 1.0    |    Purpose: Packet extraction and boundary-detection testing

chunk_2.page_content:
# 1 Introduction

This Interface Requirements Specification (IRS) defines five illustrative application-level packet formats exchanged between independent subsystems. Each packet definition identifies its sender, receiver, flow direction, field layout, encoding, and validation requirements. The examples are intentionally varied to exercise automated extraction and packet-pattern detection; they do not represent a production system.

chunk_3.page_content:
## 1.1 Purpose

This document provides packet definitions that can be extracted into a machine-readable representation and used to locate and validate packet occurrences within captured network traffic.

chunk_4.page_content:
## 1.2 Scope

This IRS specifies packet structures and interface-level validation. It does not prescribe routing, retransmission, or transport connection management.

chunk_6.page_content:
## 2.1 Subsystem and Flow Direction

Each packet definition identifies an originating subsystem (Sender) and destination subsystem (Receiver). Direction is written Sender → Receiver. The sender constructs the packet; the receiver validates and interprets it. A packet observed in the reverse direction shall not be treated as the same packet type unless explicitly specified.

chunk_7.page_content:
## 2.2 Byte Numbering and Alignment

Offsets are zero-based from the first byte of the application-level packet. Fields are serialized in table order. Every field occupies a whole number of bytes. This IRS contains no bit-packed fields.

chunk_8.page_content:
## 2.3 Boolean Representation

Every Boolean field occupies exactly one byte: 0x00 represents FALSE and 0x01 represents TRUE. All other values are invalid. A Boolean flag never occupies an individual bit.

chunk_9.page_content:
## 2.4 Numeric and Text Encoding

Integer widths and byte order are specified per field. Unless stated otherwise, multi-byte integers are little-endian. ASCII and UTF-8 fields shall use their named encodings. Text lengths are measured in encoded bytes.

chunk_10.page_content:
## 2.5 Packet Boundaries

A packet may occur at the beginning, middle, or end of a larger transport payload. Packet boundaries are determined by the signature, length fields, delimiter fields, or other framing rules in the relevant definition. One TCP payload is not assumed to equal one application packet.

chunk_11.page_content:
## 2.6 Reserved Values and Validation

Reserved bytes shall be zero. Enumerations shall contain only listed values. Receivers shall reject invalid lengths, unsupported enumeration values, invalid Boolean encodings, and failed checksums where specified.

chunk_14.page_content:
### 3.1.1 Packet Overview

Sender: Device Controller. Receiver: Network Gateway. Flow Direction: Device Controller → Network Gateway. This fixed-length packet is transmitted when a device connects to the network. It carries device identity, firmware information, capabilities, and reserved bytes.

chunk_15.page_content:
### 3.1.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Start Marker 2 ASCII Exact value: DEV!.
Packet Type 1 Unsigned 8-bit integer Exact value: 0x01.
Device ID 4 Unsigned 32-bit, little-endian Valid range: 1–4294967295.
Firmware Version 3 Byte array Three bytes in major, minor, patch order.
Device Class 2 Unsigned 16-bit, little-endian Valid range: 0–65535.
Capabilities 4 Unsigned 32-bit, little-endian Bitmask describing supported capabilities.
Reserved 2 Byte array Both bytes shall be 0x00.
End Marker 2 ASCII Exact value: !D.

chunk_16.page_content:
### 3.1.3 Length and Validation

The packet shall be exactly 20 bytes. Start Marker shall equal DEV! and End Marker shall equal !D. Packet Type shall equal 0x01. Device ID shall be non-zero and Reserved bytes shall be zero.

chunk_18.page_content:
### 3.2.1 Packet Overview

Sender: Application Controller. Receiver: Message Gateway. Flow Direction: Application Controller → Message Gateway. This variable-length packet carries a UTF-8 message. The message size is determined by the two-byte length prefix immediately preceding it.

chunk_19.page_content:
### 3.2.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Signature 3 ASCII Exact value: MSG.
Packet Type 1 Unsigned 8-bit integer Exact value: 0x02.
Message Length 2 Unsigned 16-bit, little-endian Number of encoded bytes in Message only; range 1–1024.
Message Message Length UTF-8 Must contain valid UTF-8. Its byte length shall equal Message Length.
Priority 1 Unsigned 8-bit enumeration 0 = NORMAL; 1 = HIGH; 2 = CRITICAL.
Checksum 2 Unsigned 16-bit, little-endian CRC-16 over Packet Type, Message Length, Message, and Priority.

chunk_20.page_content:
### 3.2.3 Variable-Length Validation

Total length shall equal 9 + Message Length bytes. Message Length shall be 1–1024. The Message field shall consume exactly Message Length bytes. Priority shall be 0, 1, or 2. Checksum shall match the calculated CRC. This packet has no separate footer.

chunk_22.page_content:
### 3.3.1 Packet Overview

Sender: Central Controller. Receiver: Remote Device. Flow Direction: Central Controller → Remote Device. This packet carries a textual command terminated by a line-feed delimiter. The command text is variable-length and is followed by a one-byte delimiter.

chunk_23.page_content:
### 3.3.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Signature 3 ASCII Exact value: CMD.
Packet Type 1 Unsigned 8-bit integer Exact value: 0x03.
Command ID 1 Unsigned 8-bit integer Valid range: 1–255.
Command Text Variable UTF-8 Command text ends at the first 0x0A byte. The delimiter is excluded from this field. Length shall be 1–255 encoded bytes.
Command Terminator 1 Unsigned 8-bit integer Exact value: 0x0A. Terminates Command Text.
Transaction ID 2 Unsigned 16-bit, little-endian Valid range: 0–65535.

chunk_24.page_content:
### 3.3.3 Delimiter and Length Validation

The first 0x0A byte after Command ID terminates Command Text and is represented by Command Terminator. Command Text shall contain 1–255 bytes and shall not contain an unescaped 0x0A. The receiver shall reject a packet if the delimiter is absent, the UTF-8 text is invalid, or the Transaction ID is incomplete. No footer is defined.

chunk_26.page_content:
### 3.4.1 Packet Overview

Sender: Data Acquisition Unit. Receiver: Storage Controller. Flow Direction: Data Acquisition Unit → Storage Controller. This packet transfers binary data in chunks. The Data field is variable-length and occupies the bytes remaining in the packet after its fixed metadata. The packet boundary is supplied by the enclosing record length from the transport capture or containing protocol.

chunk_27.page_content:
### 3.4.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Signature 2 ASCII Exact value: BD.
Packet Type 1 Unsigned 8-bit integer Exact value: 0x04.
Transfer ID 4 Unsigned 32-bit, little-endian Identifies the transfer.
Chunk Index 2 Unsigned 16-bit, little-endian Zero-based index; shall be less than Total Chunks.
Total Chunks 2 Unsigned 16-bit, little-endian Must be greater than zero.
Data Remaining Byte array Consumes all remaining bytes in the packet after the preceding fields. Length may be 0–4096 bytes.

chunk_28.page_content:
### 3.4.3 Remaining-Data and Length Validation

The fixed metadata occupies 11 bytes. Data shall consume all bytes remaining within the enclosing packet boundary and shall not exceed 4096 bytes. Chunk Index shall be less than Total Chunks, and Total Chunks shall be greater than zero. No checksum or footer is defined in this packet format.

chunk_30.page_content:
### 3.5.1 Packet Overview

Sender: Sensor Controller. Receiver: Monitoring Gateway. Flow Direction: Sensor Controller → Monitoring Gateway. This variable-length packet periodically reports sensor measurements. It has a synchronization header and a length field, but deliberately has no footer. The packet ends immediately after the declared payload.

chunk_31.page_content:
### 3.5.2 Field Layout
Field Size (bytes) Type / Encoding Requirements
Header 2 Byte array Exact value: 0xAA 0x55. Marks the beginning of the packet.
Packet Type 1 Unsigned 8-bit integer Exact value: 0x05.
Device ID 4 Unsigned 32-bit, little-endian Identifies the transmitting device.
Sequence Number 2 Unsigned 16-bit, little-endian Incremented for each packet sent by the same device.
Payload Length 2 Unsigned 16-bit, little-endian Number of bytes in Payload only; range 1–2048.
Payload Payload Length Byte array Contains telemetry data. Its byte length shall equal Payload Length. The packet ends immediately after this field.

chunk_32.page_content:
### 3.5.3 Packet Boundary and Length Validation

Total packet length shall equal 11 + Payload Length bytes. Payload Length shall be 1–2048. The receiver shall read exactly the declared number of payload bytes and mark the packet boundary immediately after the final payload byte. This packet has a header but no footer, terminator, or trailing checksum. The absence of a footer shall not cause rejection.

chunk_33.page_content:
# 4 Cross-Packet Interface Summary
Packet Sender Receiver Direction Length
Device Identification Device Controller Network Gateway Controller → Gateway 20 bytes
Message Transmission Application Controller Message Gateway Application → Gateway Variable
Command Request Central Controller Remote Device Controller → Device Variable
Bulk Data Transfer Data Acquisition Unit Storage Controller Acquisition → Storage 11–4107 bytes
Streaming Telemetry Sensor Controller Monitoring Gateway Sensor → Gateway 12–2059 bytes

chunk_35.page_content:
## 5.1 Fixed-Length Packets

Device Identification is fixed at 20 bytes. It requires exact-length validation, marker validation, packet-type validation, and reserved-byte checks.

chunk_36.page_content:
## 5.2 Variable-Length Packets

Message Transmission length is derived from Message Length. Command Request is terminated by the 0x0A delimiter. Bulk Data Transfer consumes the bytes remaining within its enclosing packet boundary. Streaming Telemetry length is derived from Payload Length. Receivers shall reject incomplete, malformed, or overlong candidates according to each packet definition.

chunk_37.page_content:
## 5.3 Direction Validation

Packet identity includes sender and receiver. An analyzer should retain observed source and destination endpoints and verify direction against configured subsystem-to-endpoint mappings. A byte-pattern match alone does not prove correct flow direction.

chunk_38.page_content:
# 6 Document Notes

This is an illustrative IRS for testing document extraction, structured schema generation, and packet-pattern detection. All fields are byte-aligned; no bit-packed fields are used. Every Boolean flag, if present, occupies one full byte. The five packet examples intentionally exercise fixed-size, length-prefixed, delimiter-terminated, remaining-byte, and header-only framing. The final packet (Streaming Telemetry) has a header and length field but no footer.
